articles.title: Red carpet for FPIs': Congress slams Sebi plan to ease disclosure norms for foreign investors
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress on Sunday criticised the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (Sebi) proposal to review additional disclosure requirements for
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress on Sunday criticised the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (Sebi) proposal to review additional disclosure requirements for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), saying credibility, transparency and investor protection were essential to efficient financial markets.The opposition party said the proposed changes were a step in the opposite direction and should be "buried", PTI reported.Sebi has proposed removing the additional disclosure framework that requires certain FPIs to provide granular details of entities holding ownership, economic interest or control in them. The regulator said the existing requirements go beyond beneficial ownership identification norms under anti-money laundering rules, making India's disclosure regime more stringent than those in several major global markets.Congress general secretary in-charge communications, Jairam Ramesh, said the consultation paper was issued soon after Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed industry leaders at FICCI on November 19, proposing to scrap disclosure rules introduced in August 2023 to identify opaque offshore investments in Indian companies."It is clear that the Prime Minister has little hope of reviving domestic private investment, or even FDI, and has decided instead to roll out the red carpet for foreign portfolio investors to keep the stock markets buoyant, even at the cost of market integrity," Ramesh said on X.India needed foreign investors, but not those with opaque and convoluted offshore ownership structures, he said, adding that ease of doing business could not come at the cost of capital market integrity.In August 2023, Sebi required FPIs with more than 50 per cent of their Indian equity investments in a single corporate group to provide detailed disclosures on ultimate ownership, economic interest and control, he said.The disclosures were intended to identify opaque ownership structures that could conceal concentrated control and create opportunities for market abuse, Ramesh added."Now, Sebi proposes to junk these requirements entirely. The loophole that was belatedly closed under pressure after the January 2023 revelations is being reopened," he said.Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey had earlier said the regulator would issue a consultation paper proposing further simplification of FPI regulations, including the removal of certain restrictions that are not present in other countries.Ramesh reiterated that transparency and investor protection were essential to maintaining the credibility of India's financial markets and said the proposed changes should be withdrawn.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: This 71-year-old cattleman’s farm brings in $30 million a year. He says the cattle cycle that built it is broken
articles.summary: Record beef prices used to make ranchers rebuild herds. Will Harris says land now costs too much, so he’s training new ranchers instead.
articles.body:
Cows have roamed Will Harris's 3,200-acre home farm in southwestern Georgia since 1866, when his great-grandparents got up at dawn six days a week to tend the land. They raised and slaughtered chickens, ducks, hogs, and cows, and would load up the meat in a mule-drawn wagon and drive it up the two-mile dirt road to the town of Bluffton, which had a population of 117 people at the last census, to peddle.

Now Harris, 71, has grown its operations into White Oak Pastures , a 5,700-acre farming ecosystem that he told Fortune is the largest private employer in the county and employs 170 people, almost everyone in Bluffton who isn't retired or can't work for other reasons. White Oak's workforce is larger than the town itself.

"Just about everybody in town that works, works for us," Harris said.

His business, which raises livestock, processes the meat and sells it directly to consumers, brings in $30 million a year. But Harris says the cycle that built farms like his has broken. Record cattle prices once would have sent ranchers rushing to rebuild their herds. Now the land to do it costs more than cattle can pay for, as investors and developers outbid farmers across rural Georgia. So instead of expanding, he is training new ranchers and is open to a data center coming to his county, because he isn't sure the old way of building a farm still works.

"I don't know how this is going to end," he said.

The U.S. cattle herd is at a 75-year low due to droughts and record-high operating costs, and the price of ground beef, typically the most affordable part of the animal for consumers, hit a record $6.90 per pound earlier this year . Farmland is also harder to buy as farmers are outbid by institutional investors and developers, including the data center companies spreading across rural Georgia . Harris said a data center was approved for construction in his Clay County, but hasn't started construction.

"If you can get a tremendous amount of money to sell the land, most people sell it. It happens every day, and it's not just data centers," Harris said. "The land is moving out of the hands of the farmer or cattle producers into the hands of others."

Living through the ups and downs of the cattle industry

White Oak wasn't always run the way it is now, which is as a regenerative farm, a concept Harris defines as "not breaking the cycles of nature." When Harris's father inherited the farm after World War II, he got rid of everything except for cattle and started selling calves to feedlots instead of slaughtering and delivering meat himself, using pesticides and chemical fertilizers to cut costs. Harris went to college and studied animal science, then returned to run the farm similarly for 20 years until 1995.

articles.title: Private Credit’s $100 Billion Saudi Prize Is Proving Hard to Win
articles.summary: Many private credit firms believe Saudi Arabia offers an estimated $100 billion opportunity, potentially helping transform the Middle East into one of the bi...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Many private credit firms believe Saudi Arabia offers an estimated $100 billion opportunity, potentially helping transform the Middle East into one of the biggest markets for the asset class. But deploying capital at the required scale and speed is proving difficult.

A recent $150 million financing for a little-known Saudi firm illustrates the challenge. Backed by Goldman Sachs Group Inc., HSBC Holdings Plc, Fortress Investment Group and at least three regional fund managers, and small by Wall Street standards, the deal took months to complete.

Delays over regulation, deal structure and the investor mix complicated a transaction that would have taken just weeks to put together in many other markets, according to people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified discussing private information.

That disconnect is awkward for the largest Gulf economy, which is in the midst of a multitrillion-dollar overhaul.

Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's plans to diversify away from oil require vast private investment across sectors including artificial intelligence. Just as borrowing needs rise, near-daily attacks by the Houthis are adding to the pressure, weighing on economic activity, exacerbating a liquidity crunch and denting investor confidence.

"The conflict has fundamentally reinforced the strategic importance of private capital for Saudi Arabia," said Atefeh Ebadian, chief economist and investment strategist at Dubai-based Symax Group, whose work focuses on Gulf economies and evaluating private investment opportunities. "It has also changed the urgency."

Yet, regulatory uncertainty, licensing timelines and rules around local presence are impeding progress and slowing the flow of capital, according to more than a dozen fund managers. Even firms that clear those hurdles face difficulty deploying money, they said, pointing to a pipeline dominated by small companies and returns that may not always adequately compensate for the extra effort and risk.

Saudi Arabia has historically been the engine of private capital fundraising in the Middle East, accounting for more than half of all regional funds closed since 2015, according to a report by BlackRock, which cited data from Preqin. Now, at least six fund managers said raising money from investors for local deals had become harder.

articles.title: The Stock Market Is Doing Something for Only the 5th Time This Century, and History Says It's Obvious What Comes Next for Stocks
articles.summary: If things seem too perfect for investors, they often are.
articles.body:
With less than six weeks left in 2026, investors have little to complain about. The mature-stock-driven Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI), broad-based S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC), and tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) have all catapulted to several record highs this year, driven by the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure build-out, better-than-expected corporate earnings, and initial public offering euphoria.

While Wall Street's major stock indexes have made a habit of climbing the proverbial wall of worry and rising over the long term, history also makes clear that bull markets don't last forever. If things seem too perfect for investors, they often are .

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Though any number of headwinds can knock the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite off their respective pedestals, one stands out. We're currently witnessing the stock market do something for only the fifth time this century, and history doesn't mince its words about what comes next for stocks.

Stock valuations have entered rarefied (and unsustainable) territory

Despite a parabolic move in outstanding margin debt sending all the wrong signals, the biggest worry for Wall Street and investors is premium stock valuations.

To be clear, past events can't guarantee what the future holds. Nevertheless, history has shown a tendency to rhyme on Wall Street more often than not, making it an excellent teaching tool for those investors willing to listen.

Most investors rely on the time-tested price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio when evaluating individual companies or the broader market. While the P/E ratio, which is derived using trailing 12-month earnings per share (EPS), is incredibly useful for quickly sizing up mature businesses, it can lose its utility entirely when recessions occur and EPS turns negative.

For Wall Street's broad-market stock indexes, the S&P 500's Shiller P/E Ratio, also known as the Cyclically Adjusted P/E Ratio (CAPE Ratio), is a far superior valuation tool. The Shiller P/E is based on average inflation-adjusted EPS over the trailing 10 years, meaning recessions won't render it useless.

Though economists introduced the S&P 500's Shiller P/E Ratio less than four decades ago, it's been backtested to January 1871. Over these 156 years, the average reading is a relatively modest 17.45. As of the closing bell on Nov. 17, it was 38.76, or 122% above this long-term average.

articles.title: IIT Delhi alumnus’ startup sues Apple for Rs 1,500 crore over NameDrop feature
articles.summary: IIT Delhi alumnus’ startup GG Technologies sues Apple in Bombay HC for Rs 1,500 crore over NameDrop, alleging patent infringement and seeking an injunction.
articles.body: BENGALURU: A startup founded by IIT Delhi alumnus Gaurav Goel has sued Apple in the Bombay High Court over its NameDrop contact-sharing feature. GG Technologies is seeking Rs 1,500 crore in damages for alleged patent infringement.The US-incorporated company, which developed the StayTouch app, said it filed the Indian suit in October after unsuccessful mediation. It is also seeking an injunction against products it alleges infringe its patent.NameDrop allows users to share contact information by bringing compatible iPhones and Apple Watches close together. Apple announced the feature in June 2023 as part of iOS 17.GG Technologies said its Indian patent, titled Method and System for Proximity-Based Contact Transfer, was granted on July 27, 2024. Its first US provisional patent application was filed in May 2019, the company said.Goel, a former Goldman Sachs investment banker, founded GG Technologies in 2018. The company launched StayTouch’s global beta in 2019 as an alternative to exchanging business cards.The company said two technical experts assessed its patent and NameDrop’s functionality using Apple’s published documentation and their own examination of the feature. It said their reports identified substantial technical similarities in how devices detect each other, obtain user consent and let users choose which contact details to share.GG Technologies said it has not licensed the technology to Apple or received royalties. It also alleged that some prospective partners were reluctant to pursue discussions because Apple already offered a similar feature. It did not identify the partners or quantify the lost business in its response.The startup said it has also filed two patent suits against Apple in the US, in April and November.Separately, the US International Trade Commission announced an investigation on August 28 following a July 28 complaint by GG Technologies. The commission named Apple as the respondent. The startup has sought orders restricting imports and sales of allegedly infringing devices in the US, according to the announcement.The commission said opening the investigation did not amount to a decision on the merits of the case. GG Technologies said no final finding on infringement has been made in the proceedings so far.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: GPU prices are rising for Nvidia's older chips even as the stock keeps going down: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Investors can't get out of Nvidia fast enough. The companies running AI can't get enough of its chips.
articles.body:
Investors can't get out of Nvidia ( NVDA ) fast enough . The companies running AI can't get enough of its chips.

The price to rent an Nvidia H100, a chip it started shipping in 2022, climbed nearly 60% over the past year to about $3.11 an hour, according to Silicon Data's H100 rental index . Fine wine, the collectible that's supposed to get better with age, rose about 2% over the same stretch, based on the Liv-ex Fine Wine 100 .

Nvidia stock, meanwhile, has lost nearly half its value since its October record, a staggering loss of over $2.7 trillion in market value . It sank 14% on Friday alone, its worst day since the DeepSeek sell-off in January 2025 and its worst week ever, as the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) fell more than 5%.

Asked on Deirdre Bosa Live on Thursday whether AI is in a bubble, AMP founder Anjney Midha didn't hesitate. "GPU wastage bubble, not AI bubble," he said.

CoreWeave ( CRWV ), which rents out Nvidia chips by the hour, is seeing the same thing. Its "pricing for Amperes and Hoppers increased 30% to 50% quarter-over-quarter," CEO Mike Intrator said on the company's third quarter call , referring to the families behind Nvidia's older A100 and H100 chips.

Credit where it's due. A year ago, Michael Burry's hedge fund disclosed bets against Nvidia and Palantir ( PLTR ). Both stocks are down more than 30% since.

His case went further, though. Burry argued that Big Tech was stretching out the depreciation of its AI chips — how fast it writes down their value — and understating that cost by $176 billion from 2026 through 2028. He called it "one of the more common frauds of the modern era."

The rental market hasn't gotten the memo. CoreWeave is "signing multi-year commitments extending beyond the GPU's depreciable lives," Intrator said. Firmer rents also prop up the chips' value as collateral, welcome news for lenders that hold the title on billions of dollars of Nvidia hardware .

On Sept. 11, Burry told subscribers to his Substack that "just about every single case of fine wine sitting in a London bonded warehouse can be a short position on the U.S. dollar." The US dollar index has climbed about 5% since bottoming that week.

Renting H100s is far from a sure thing. Some of the rise in price may be a "credit crunch in disguise," as lenders finance less against chips and push buyers to rent, according to ZeroHedge . H100 rent is also still below where it stood in September 2024, when Silicon Data's index begins.

But for perspective, renting two H100s around the clock now costs about $4,540 a month. The median Manhattan apartment rented for $4,900 in September, according to Miller Samuel .

articles.title: Bengaluru businessman declares Rs 19.26 crore income, but tax department seizes Rs 4.10 crore cash and Rs 8.11 crore jewellery including 751.52 grams gold and decides to tax him at special rate; ITAT gives relief
articles.summary: If you have business income then it is very important to keep all your records in place, accounting for all your income sources.
articles.body: If you have business income then it is very important to keep all your records in place, accounting for all your income sources. A businessman in Bengaluru found himself facing a tax notice after raids revealed cash in his locker which the Income Tax Department treated as unexplained.He eventually managed to get relief from the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal. Here’s how the case unfolded.What the case is about:In 2018, the Income Tax Department conducted searches at a man’s residence and on his locker. During the operation, officials reportedly recovered Rs 3.9 crore in cash from the locker and another Rs 20 lakh from his house.The locker also contained jewellery valued at Rs 8.11 crore, including 751.52 grams of gold and 81.470 carats of diamonds. The jewellery was seized. Two watches worth Rs 16.25 lakh were also found in the locker and confiscated.Then, the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) in Bengaluru classified the total cash of Rs 4.1 crore as unexplained money under Section 69A and proposed taxing it at a special rate.The AO also asked the man to explain the source of the gold and diamond jewellery. Although he submitted an explanation, the officer was not satisfied with it and treated the jewellery as unexplained assets.The man pointed out that he had filed his income tax return (ITR), declaring income of Rs 19.26 crore, of which Rs 18.11 crore was reported as business income. He maintained that the cash recovered from his locker represented business earnings from earlier years through real estate commissions and money lending activities. According to him, the Rs 20 lakh found at his residence belonged to various family members.The AO rejected these submissions. Explaining the jewellery and diamonds, the man said their value, along with that of the watches, had already been included in the business income disclosed for the previous year. He further stated that the jewellery kept in the locker had been disclosed in the wealth tax returns filed by him and his family members.Regarding the two watches, the man submitted that his sister had gifted them to him and that their value had also been included in his ITR as business income. The AO, however, did not accept these explanations and classified the value of the jewellery and watches as unexplained investment under Section 69.Why ITAT Bangalore gave reliefThe man subsequently filed an appeal before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Bengaluru. On November 3, 2026, the tribunal ruled in his favour on the disputed assets, and asked the Income Tax Department to treat the seized cash as his business income.ITAT observed that the man had established that he earned business income and that the seized cash and jewellery had been reported as business income in the income tax return filed for Assessment Year 2019-20. The supporting documents and other evidence were also consistent with his explanation.The tribunal further noted that the Assessing Officer had not produced any additional material to establish that Amarlal earned income from other sources that could be assessed as unexplained money or investment under Sections 69 and 69A. Copies of the wealth tax returns filed by Amarlal and his family members supported his claim that the jewellery had been disclosed in earlier filings.Chartered Accountant Rohhit Saluja told ET that ITAT Bangalore held that cash and jewellery seized during an Income Tax Department search cannot automatically be classified as black money or unexplained investments under Sections 69 and 69A of the Income-tax Act, 1961.Saluja explained that the tribunal's decision rested on five key considerations.First, the man had explained the nature of the seized cash in his statement recorded under Section 132(4).Second, his audited financial statements and income tax returns showed that business activities were his primary source of income.Third, the cash and jewellery recovered during the search had been accounted for as business income for the relevant assessment year.Fourth, his wealth tax returns for Assessment Year 2015-16 showed that he had disclosed jewellery in earlier years.Fifth, he had submitted a notarised affidavit of withdrawal on July 23, 2018, just three days after the search.According to Saluja, the Assessing Officer had not produced independent evidence to establish that the seized assets came from sources other than Amarlal's business activities.On this basis, the ITAT Bengaluru Bench held that the assets should be treated as business income and taxed at the applicable regular rates, rather than the special rate prescribed under Section 115BBE. The appeal was consequently allowed.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Strong Earnings Prove No Match for the Crumbling AI Trade
articles.summary: For years, a strong earnings season has given Wall Street something to fall back on. But the crumbling artificial-intelligence trade has ripped away that sup...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- For years, a strong earnings season has given Wall Street something to fall back on. But the crumbling artificial-intelligence trade has ripped away that support.

Companies in the S&P 500 Index just delivered a second-consecutive quarter of profit growth in excess of 30%, defying fears rising costs would slow earnings. Instead of rallying, the index slumped, signaling strong results alone aren't enough to protect mounting anxiety around the AI trade.

Between JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s results that kicked off the announcement season in October and Walmart Inc.'s report on Thursday that marked its unofficial end, the S&P 500 slumped 8.1%, posting its worst earnings-season run since 2011. The index fell another 3.7% Friday and entered correction territory, down 12% from its recent high on Oct. 6.

The strong earnings cycle was not enough to support the stock market as a Democratic sweep of US midterm elections raised the prospect of tighter regulation of data centers, threatening a central pillar of the artificial intelligence boom — not to mention the S&P 500's future profit growth. The shock ouster of Nvidia Corp. founder Jensen Huang also rattled nervous investors.

"There's a lot of anxiety," said Daniel Farley, chief investment officer at US Bank Wealth Management. "Earnings growth will continue but just not as good of a rate. I think the market is going to continue to struggle with that."

Upside surprises were smaller than in prior quarters, data compiled by Bloomberg Intelligence show. Firms are also returning less to shareholders. Data from 22V Research LLC show 53% of S&P 500 earnings were spent on dividends and buybacks, the lowest such reading since at least 1990, as far back as data go.

Concerns that earnings growth has peaked haven't disappeared. They've merely been delayed to 2027.

Here are five things we learned as firms reported third-quarter results.

Investors concerned about tech companies' overspending on AI were quick to sell if third-quarter results didn't meet expectations. Google-parent Alphabet Inc., Facebook-owner Meta Platforms Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. all slumped after third-quarter reports showed negative free cash flow, heightening concerns about how much they were spending on AI.

articles.title: Efficiency Jobs Fall Just As AI And Hormuz Make Them Matter Most
articles.summary: U.S. energy efficiency jobs fell for the first time since 2020 as tax credits vanished, just as AI, power bills and the Hormuz crisis make them vital.
articles.body:
When families crowd into the kitchen this Thanksgiving, the oven won't be the only thing working overtime. Furnaces and heat pumps across much of the country are kicking on for the season, and in millions of homes a good share of that heat will slip out through thin attic insulation, drafty windows and leaky ductwork. Until last New Year's Eve, homeowners could get 30% of the cost of fixing those problems back at tax time. That credit is gone. And the workers who do the fixing are starting to go with it.

The U.S. energy efficiency sector lost 21,441 jobs in 2025, a 0.9% decline and its first drop since the pandemic year of 2020, according to the latest Energy Efficiency Jobs in America report from the Building Performance Foundation. That sounds modest. But energy efficiency employs more Americans than the entire oil and gas industry. It also includes all power plants, including wind and solar farms. It is shrinking just as the country needs it most: household power bills are climbing, AI data centers are straining the grid, and the cheapest megawatt is still the one a utility never has to generate.

"Energy efficiency is fundamental to the health of the U.S. economy. It's the biggest employer in the energy sector, saves consumers money on their energy bills, which in turn improves housing affordability, and supports U.S. energy independence," said Paul Francisco, CEO of the Building Performance Foundation, in a statement released with the report. "After four years of solid employment gains, it is disappointing to see the sector lose jobs."

The sector employed 2.36 million people last year, a quarter of the U.S. energy workforce and twice as many as oil and gas, coal and nuclear combined. They are insulators, HVAC technicians, energy auditors, window installers and the factory workers who build ENERGY STAR equipment. Their jobs can't be shipped overseas, and they pay well: wages run 18% to 23% above the national average and rose 2.8% last year, nearly double the 1.5% gain across all industries.

The losses were uneven. California alone shed 8,754 jobs, about 40% of the national decline, followed by Maryland, Illinois, Wisconsin and Massachusetts. Meanwhile, 17 states added efficiency jobs, led by New Mexico, Nevada and Idaho, and factories making energy-saving appliances, insulation and windows added about 10,000 jobs, a 3% gain. The broader energy economy lost about 86,000 jobs, or 1%, according to the Department of Energy's annual employment survey , which the efficiency report draws on; only the grid, meaning power lines, pipelines and battery storage, added them in any number.

articles.title: Record Rs 1.22 lakh crore foreign inflows: Is India becoming the world's 'anti-AI' trade?
articles.summary: Was the artificial intelligence (AI)-led stock rally a bubble all along? Has it burst?
articles.body: Was the artificial intelligence (AI)-led stock rally a bubble all along? Has it burst? And, is India which suffered sharp foreign outflows over the last two years for the lack of an AI story, now becoming the new favourite? Is India the world’s ‘anti-AI’ trade?Global stock markets tell a revealing story: Since the US-mid term elections, the selloff in AI-related stocks has intensified, exacerbated by the unfolding crisis at Nvidia. Since then, Nasdaq is down 7.98%. Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have remained net buyers on every trading day this month, barring the Muhurat trading session. articles.title: HBO Max and Paramount+ Bundle Faces Antitrust Lawsuit
articles.summary: After two dismissals, subscribers may have one last shot at their antitrust case. Can their amended complaint keep the streaming merger fight alive?
articles.body:
Paramount's $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery is already complete, but subscribers are heading back to court to challenge what happens next. A newly amended federal lawsuit targets the company's plans to bundle HBO Max and Paramount+, arguing that putting both streaming services under one owner could mean higher prices, fewer choices, and less competition.

According to The Hollywood Reporter , consumers refiled their antitrust complaint Thursday in federal court in California, seeking to unwind the blockbuster acquisition. The lawsuit points to a planned HBO Max and Paramount+ bundle arriving in early 2027 as evidence that Skydance is moving toward eliminating competition between two previously independent streaming platforms.

The argument is straightforward: Before the merger, customers unhappy with HBO Max could cancel and switch to Paramount+, or vice versa. Now, both services belong to the same company, even if they continue operating under separate names.

Skydance's streaming services "may retain distinct names and interfaces, but both now answer to one owner and its combined financial interests," the complaint states.

The plaintiffs argue that the arrangement gives Skydance less incentive to compete against itself on subscription prices, exclusive programming, or customer value.

"The consumer may still choose between two brands, but no longer has the choice between those two independent sellers," the lawsuit states.

And Skydance executives haven't exactly hidden their plans to bring the platforms closer together.

"Long-term, the plan is basically to bring them together," CEO David Ellison said last month after Paramount completed its Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition on Oct. 6.

The company recently outlined plans to achieve at least $6 billion in annual savings through layoffs, real estate consolidation, increased reliance on artificial intelligence, and changes to its content operations.

articles.title: The AI boom is fueling demand for skilled trades
articles.summary: An expected 1.7 million skilled trade jobs will open each year in the next decade, according to a recent report.
articles.body:
On weekdays from 5 a.m. to 1 p.m., Marty Tougher clocks in at the construction site of a new building at UPMC Presbyterian, a 900-bed hospital in downtown Pittsburgh.

Depending on the day, he might work on framing — building the skeletons of walls and ceilings — or drywalling to cover that frame with gypsum panels to create finished surfaces.

"It's fun," Tougher, 21, told Yahoo Finance. "I like working with my hands."

Two years ago, Tougher decided to pursue a career as a carpenter, and he's now in his third year in a carpentry apprentice program at the Keystone Mountain Lakes Regional Council of Carpenters in Pittsburgh. The program is tuition-free, combining paid on-the-job training with classroom instruction.

In western Pennsylvania, nonresidential construction is booming with no sign of abating, said Jeff Nobers, executive director of the Builders Guild of Western Pennsylvania.

In high demand are operating engineers, boilermakers, steam fitters, carpenters, plumbers, and electricians. Even some of the trades that weren't necessarily hot a few years back, such as bricklayers, cement masons, roofers, and insulators, are needed again.

"These big billion-dollar data center and natural gas plant projects, for example, require all of them," he said.

Trade jobs are getting renewed traction, driven by infrastructure demand across the country for massive projects like AI data centers, natural gas plants, and power grid expansion.

More than 18 million Americans work in skilled trades, and an expected 1.7 million skilled trade jobs will open each year in the next decade, according to a recent report .

Employment of plumbers, pipefitters, and steamfitters, for example, is projected to grow 7% from 2025 to 2035, much faster than the average for all occupations, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. That adds up to roughly 42,000 openings each year. Plus, retiring workers in these fields are rapidly opening up positions for younger workers.

Apprenticeship programs like the one Tougher is part of generally run from three to five years. Students spend 10% of their time in the classroom, or 200 hours a year, learning specific trade skills along with local building codes, blueprint reading, mathematics, and more. The bulk of their time, 1,800 hours, is on the job, Nobers said.

"What I like about working on construction projects is you can see the progress, how it all comes together, and the work is always changing," said Tougher. "You're not just doing the same thing over and over."

articles.title: I'm a Mortgage Lender: What the Fed's Rate Increase Means for First-Time Homebuyers
articles.summary: The Fed’s September rate hike doesn’t directly set mortgage rates. Here’s what it could mean for first-time buyers and whether to buy now or wait.
articles.body:
The target range for the federal funds rate rose to 3.75% to 4.00% on Sept. 17, 2026, per the Federal Reserve Bank of New York . This is a quarter of a percentage point increase from what it was before. That same day, the effective federal funds rate (EFFR) increased from 3.63% to 3.88%.

It's easy to see a rate hike like this and think it'll cause mortgage rates to rise as well. However, this isn't entirely true. The EFFR does have an impact on interest rates, but it's not a one-for-one relationship.

MoneyLion asked Darren Tooley, senior loan officer at Cornerstone Financial Services , what the rate increase means for first-time buyers and whether it should factor into your decision to purchase now as opposed to waiting. Here's what he said.

How the Rate Hike Impacts Mortgage Rates

Contrary to popular belief, the Fed doesn't control the interest rates banks and other lenders set. So, just because the effective rate has risen, that doesn't mean mortgage rates will now rise.

"There is a big misconception that when the Federal Reserve raises or lowers rates, mortgage rates automatically increase or decrease by the same amount," Tooley said. "Mortgage rates are based on the trading of mortgage-backed securities (MBS), which are influenced more directly by the bond market, inflation expectations and the overall outlook for the economy."

Worth noting is that mortgage lenders don't change their rates on a dime. That's because home loans are a type of long-term debt. The rates you see are based on projections of future economic conditions. Just like the Federal funds rate, they can change, but not necessarily overnight.

Your credit profile as a borrower also impacts the mortgage rate you get. The better your credit (and income), the better your rate tends to be. Other factors, like having a larger down payment or paying discount points, could also lower your interest rate.

For you as a first-time homebuyer, the Fed's rate hike could (indirectly) mean the following.

Higher monthly payments (leading to affordability concerns)

Decreased purchasing power (with higher loan costs)

Potentially more opportunities on the market for the more financially prepared buyer

"The rate hike in September sent a clear message that inflation isn't beaten yet and since inflation is one of the biggest indicators of the economy's health, it did impact mortgage rates," Tooley explained. "So, while the Fed's decisions to raise or lower rates don't directly correlate to mortgage rates, those decisions affect the direction of the economy, which has an underlying influence on how mortgage rates respond."

articles.title: US seeks answers on Nvidia's sale of chips to China, Bessent says
articles.summary: By Katharine Jackson WASHINGTON, Nov 22 (Reuters) - The US is seeking answers from Nvidia on its chip sales to China and will find out who was in charge of c...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Nov 22 (Reuters) - The US is seeking answers from Nvidia on its chip sales to China and will find out who ‌was in charge of compliance at the company formerly led by ‌Jensen Huang, who resigned following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent ​said on Sunday.

"We've been in touch with the temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do need answers. ... It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was," Bessent told ‌the CBS program "Face the Nation."

Reports ⁠about Huang's relationship with a woman whom US intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy and his extramarital affair with a ⁠company executive led to his resignation and investigations by US regulators and the FBI, congressional action, an internal review and a proposed investor class-action lawsuit.

Days after Huang's resignation, President ​Donald ​Trump's administration issued a rule to further ​restrict China's access to advanced AI ‌chips from companies like Nvidia, tightening controls ahead of Trump's trip to China last week for talks with President Xi Jinping.

Bessent said the chipmaker's board of directors is working to determine what had happened, and he expressed confidence that it would "come up with some very fulsome and robust answers."

"We do need to see ‌who was in charge of compliance there," Bessent ​said. "We will see which level of the business ​knew about this. Was it ​at the lower levels? Was it at the middle level? Did ‌it go all the way to ​the top?"

Trump said on ​Friday that he would like to see Huang apologize and return to Nvidia. Asked whether he agreed with Trump, Bessent said more information is needed.

"I ​think we have to ‌see where the buck stops," Bessent said.

Nvidia board Chairman Harvey Jones has ​said the board will not rehire Huang.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos predicts Amazon will eventually 'go bankrupt' and shares 30-year rule behind it
articles.summary: The Amazon founder said big companies rarely make it 100 years, then told employees how to buy more time.
articles.body:
Founders usually talk about their companies like proud parents at a graduation. One of the richest men on the planet once stood in front of his own staff and talked about the funeral.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos gave that answer when an employee asked where the company was headed. He said Amazon would one day go under, and he had a number in mind for how long giants like it usually last.

"Amazon is not too big to fail," Bezos said at an all-hands meeting in Seattle in November 2018, according to a recording heard by CNBC . "In fact, I predict one day Amazon will fail. Amazon will go bankrupt. If you look at large companies, their lifespans tend to be 30-plus years, not a hundred-plus years."

That's the 30-year rule, and Bezos applied it to his own company.

The employee's question was about what Amazon could learn from recent retail bankruptcies like Sears, according to CNBC . The 132-year-old chain had filed for Chapter 11 weeks earlier, in October 2018. Toys "R" Us had shuttered its last U.S. stores that June.

Amazon was 24 at the time, founded in July 1994. By Bezos' own math, the company was already most of the way to its expiration date.

The data backs up his gloomy math. Companies on the S&P 500 in the late 1970s stayed on the index for an average of 30 to 35 years, according to growth strategy firm Innosight , which forecast that the figure would shrink to 15 to 20 years this decade.

So Amazon is mortal. So what? Bezos' answer was that the job isn't avoiding the end. It's pushing it back.

He told employees to "obsess over customers," according to CNBC.

"If we start to focus on ourselves, instead of focusing on our customers, that will be the beginning of the end," Bezos said. "We have to try and delay that day for as long as possible."

He had already spelled out what happens when a company stops doing that.

"Day 2 is stasis," Bezos wrote in his 2016 letter to shareholders , published in April 2017. "Followed by irrelevance. Followed by excruciating, painful decline. Followed by death. And that is why it is always Day 1."

Day 1 meant acting like a startup that has to earn every customer, even at a company Amazon's size. In the same letter, Bezos pointed to Prime as proof. "No customer ever asked Amazon to create the Prime membership program, but it sure turns out they wanted it," he wrote.

articles.title: Stocks are 'on fire sale' as Anthropic IPO fails to calm AI trade jitters
articles.summary: Anthropic's public debut did little to calm the stock market as the AI trade unravels.
articles.body:
Anthropic's ( ANT ) IPO did little to stem the AI trade's meltdown this week, as the Nasdaq erased its year-to-date gains, leaving it roughly 18% off its October all-time high.

The biggest winners of the artificial intelligence boom are down double-digit percentages for the week, and even more so over the past month, as seen on Yahoo Finance's AlphaSpace chart.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares are down 42% over the past four weeks, as Jensen Huang's departure as CEO intensified pressure on an already shaky chip sector. Peer AMD ( AMD ) is down roughly 20%. Meanwhile, memory maker Micron ( MU ) has fallen more than 33% over the past month and is down 50% from its June all-time high.

Concerns over tighter data center regulations, restrictions on chip exports to China, and broader financing worries have weighed across the sector.

Although Anthropic's IPO wasn't the clearing event markets had hoped for, some strategists see the debut as a net positive for the AI trade.

"We're finally getting details with respect to what's underneath the curtain" when it comes to the AI developers, Raymond James Investment Management chief market strategist Matt Orton said on Yahoo Finance's Market Hang.

"Hopefully the market will kind of start to calm down and realize that there's a lot of really high-quality companies that are on fire sale right now," he added.

Orton wouldn't compare the meltdown seen in the AI trade to the 2000 dot-com bubble, noting that startups are now staying private longer as they receive the financing they need and that some of the selling may be year-end positioning to protect gains.

"The market is really healthy," Orton said.

Nomura's Charlie McElligott points out that in recent sessions investors have been broadly selling rather than just rotating into defensive sectors. Instead of "buying the dip," money is moving out of equities and into cash and US Treasurys, where prices move inversely with yields. On Friday, the 10-year Treasury ( ^TNX ) yield sank by 14 basis points to 4.91%.

McElligott will be watching this upcoming week, when computer-driven, volatility-targeted funds could step in and buy, testing whether the recent sell-off is just a dip or a sign that investors are heading for the exits.

"IF by early next week we find the Equities tape STILL unable to stabilize and move higher…it's telling me there are larger structural forces at play, that somebody wants OUT," wrote McElligott on Friday.

UBS strategists noted they still expect the S&P 500 to reach new highs in the months ahead. But "the risk-reward is becoming more balanced," David Lefkowitz, UBS head of US equities, wrote on Friday.

The firm recently downgraded US equities from Attractive to Neutral.

Strategists advise reducing tech concentration and moving into intermediate-duration bonds, such as 2- to 10-year maturities, as they can offer strong yields and portfolio protection.

articles.title: Goldman Traders See Entry Point in US Stocks But Warn of Risks
articles.summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s trading desk says last week’s selloff has created an attractive opportunity to snap up US stocks. Still, the bank cautions that ov...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Goldman Sachs Group Inc.'s trading desk says last week's selloff has created an attractive opportunity to snap up US stocks. Still, the bank cautions that overall investor positioning remains elevated, signaling the broader capitulation needed for a meaningful rally could be missing.

The bank's Volatility Panic Index spiked to 9.8 out of 10 on Friday, approaching historical extremes. Hedge funds have aggressively reduced exposure, with the bank's prime brokerage data showing a third consecutive week of global equity selling. Short sales outpaced long purchases by 1.5 to 1, while US single-stock shorting reached the highest level since June 2022 on a weekly level. Fundamental long-short funds have pushed a measure of their risk appetite known as net leverage to 42.3%, the lowest level in a year.

Hedge funds' equity unwind has become "quite extended" and markets are nearing a "tactical entry" point, the bank's trading desk wrote in a note to clients on Sunday. But a few major headwinds are still in place: the broader stock-market positioning remains elevated, the Federal Reserve is expected to keep raising interest rates and future profits from massive artificial intelligence investments remain uncertain.

"Generally speaking, panic like we've recently seen has been a good opportunity to start adding risk," the bank's traders wrote in the note. "But there are two important differences with today's setup that we're getting pushback on."

The first major risk to a meaningful rally in US equities is the Fed, according to Goldman. The bank's traders pointed to parallels with the fourth quarter of 2018, when the Fed's tightening cycle and weakening risk appetite pushed US stocks to the brink of a bear market. After a sharp selloff in October 2018, the S&P 500 proceeded to fall another 6.8% before reaching a bottom. In the five historical instances when Goldman's panic index exceeded 9 during a rate-hiking cycle, the S&P 500 has gained just 0.4% on average in the next three months.

The second important variable is broader investor positioning, which hasn't followed hedge funds in slashing equity exposure. Goldman's US Equity Sentiment Indicator, which tracks nine positioning measures across groups like mutual funds and retail investors, remains in the 75th percentile of historical observations. Investors have poured nearly $170 billion into US equity mutual funds and exchange-traded funds since the start of the fourth quarter, while asset managers' equity futures exposure sits in the 82nd percentile of readings going back 10 years ago.

articles.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.), who is likely to become the Speaker of the House next year, said Sunday that he will take action to bar lawmakers from trading stocks “very early” in the next Congress.

“So, well, listen, we’ve got to clean up the mess in Washington. That means the Congress, that means the Supreme Court and that also means with respect to the administration,” Jeffries told CBS News’s Margaret Brennan on “Face the Nation.”

“And we should begin by dealing with our own house, which is why very early on in the new Congress, House Democrats are going to move to ban members of Congress from trading stock,” he added.

Jeffries’s comments come after Democrats won back the House and Senate in the midterm elections earlier this month, even securing wins in regions where they have historically struggled, like Texas and Kansas.

In late September , Senate Democrats blocked a bill to prevent members of Congress from purchasing new stocks of publicly traded companies, saying the legislation wasn’t defensive enough against possible corruption.

The Stop Insider Trading Act sunk in a 53-47 vote, with none of the Democrats backing and 60 votes required for it to advance.

Last Wednesday, House Democrats nominated Jeffries to take up the role of Speaker, placing him another step closer to being the chamber’s first Black Speaker. Jeffries garnered 251 votes for the role from his caucus, while 11 people did not support him.

Beyond banning congressional stock trading, other priorities for Jeffries next year include reversing Medicaid cuts adopted by Republicans last year and expanding ObamaCare tax credits, with Republicans allowing them to expire at the beginning of 2026.

articles.body: US Democrats have secured their largest House majority in more than three decades, winning at least 258 seats in the 435-member chamber after a closely contested North Carolina race was called in their favour. The tally matches the party's result in 1992, when Bill Clinton was elected president, and exceeds its 257-seat haul in 2008.The milestone came on Sunday after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican incumbent Virginia Foxx in North Carolina's 5th Congressional District. Foxx conceded after a recount confirmed Hubbard's lead, giving Democrats their 44th seat gain in the November 3 midterm elections.Hubbard led Foxx by just 331 votes after the initial count, a margin of less than one per cent of the roughly 287,000 ballots cast. Foxx, who was first elected to Congress in 2004 and chairs the powerful House Rules Committee, requested a recount under North Carolina's election rules.The recount failed to overturn the result, with Hubbard's lead standing at 330 votes. Foxx called him on Sunday to concede. "The peaceful transition of elected office from one person to another is one of the true hallmarks of our system of government, and I am proud to be a citizen of a nation that prizes fair and free elections," Foxx said in a statement.Hubbard, a former journalist, thanked Foxx for her service.Four House races still to be decidedWith Hubbard's victory, Democrats have secured at least 258 House seats, while Republicans have won at least 173. Four races remain unresolved: one each in Minnesota and Tennessee, and two in Louisiana, where runoffs are scheduled for December.The Democratic tally is their strongest since 1992 and gives the party a sizeable margin over Republicans. The party has gained 44 seats so far, surpassing the 40 seats it picked up in President Donald Trump's first midterm election in 2018.Overall, the results mean that Democrats control both the House and Senate when the new Congress convenes in January, setting up a divided government with Trump remaining in the White House. Democrats have secured a 56-seat majority in the Senate, their biggest advantage in more than a decade.The party is preparing a 100-day agenda focused on the cost of living, including efforts to reverse Republican cuts to Medicaid and restore expired tax credits under the Affordable Care Act.Democrats have also pledged to use their majority and congressional subpoena powers to investigate the Trump administration, including the president's financial dealings. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to become the first Black speaker of the House if elected on January 3, 2027, has not ruled out seeking Trump's impeachment for a third time."This is a historic moment for our country. This is one of the largest classes we have seen," progressive Democratic Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez said, describing the result as "a mandate for change".Representative Tom Suozzi said Democrats should devote 75 per cent of their time to affordability and 25 per cent to accountability, arguing that investigations should be linked to their impact on ordinary Americans.The party's expanded majority is expected to give its leadership greater room to pass legislation despite differences within its ranks. Republican leader Jim Jordan, meanwhile, has vowed to oppose the Democratic agenda and work towards regaining power."Over the next two years, House Republicans will fight for American families," Jordan said.Overall, Democrats have gained 44 House seats so far, compared with Republicans' losses, leaving the GOP with at least 173 seats against the Democrats' 258. The result marks a sharp reversal from the narrow Republican majority that had often struggled to push legislation through the House. Four races are still outstanding, with two Louisiana contests heading to December runoffs.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Go public or stay private: Tata Sons gears up for decision this week
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Tata Sons is heading into one of its most consequential weeks in decades.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Tata Sons is heading into one of its most consequential weeks in decades. When its board meets on November 26, it will confront a choice that could determine whether the Tata Group's closely held holding company remains private or opens its doors to the public.It has to pick between two competing paths: RBI's Nov 16 letter reiterating that Tata Sons must comply with rules governing upper-layer non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) to list its shares, and Tata Trusts' Sept 28 proposal to merge two companies into Tata Sons, which would take the combined entity outside the NBFC and core investment company (CIC) framework and avoid a listing.The six-member board is already divided, with Trusts chairman Noel Tata, a director of Tata Sons, opposed to an IPO while the other five directors favour compliance with RBI's listing requirement. The divide extends to Trusts, where trustees including Noel's older half-brother Jimmy Tata, Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh, are in favour of an IPO.RBI's latest missive and Trusts' merger plan both followed the dramatic Sept 17 Tata Sons board meet, where almost all directors argued in favour of compliance.Noel, however, maintained that compliance need not mean a listing and the company should examine alternatives.The RBI letter makes no reference to the merger proposal, but it refers to the Tata Sons board meeting and says it understood the company's Oct 6 request for guidance on listing. Noel has questioned whether Tata Sons has sought the RBI's guidance on his merger proposal and asked the company to evaluate it and present its pros and cons to the board this week.Senior advocate Harish Salve who advises Tata Sons and chairman N Chandrasekaran has publicly endorsed a listing. "If the RBI says go list yourself, there is no use saying my shareholders don't agree," he said, maintaining that going public would bring greater transparency and prevent the company from being paralysed by disagreements among Tata Trusts trustees.Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, representing Trusts, has argued for their primacy as Tata Sons' controlling shareholder. He said the company cannot have a "runaway board" taking major decisions in disagreement with the Trusts. Tata Sons is the only company among the relevant upper-layer NBFCs to remain unlisted.If both items are put to a vote, the outcome is expected to be 5:1 in each case, but with Noel being in a minority: voting against an IPO and in favour of the Trusts' merger proposal. That, however, would reopen the dispute over Article 121 of Tata Sons' Articles of Association.Noel's position is that a resolution under Article 121 must secure the affirmative vote of a majority of Trust-nominated directors. With Noel and Srinivasan as the two Trust nominees, the Trusts contend that both must vote in favour. Tata Sons disputes this interpretation, maintaining that if the two Trust nominees vote in opposite directions, Article 121 allows the chairman of the meeting to exercise a casting vote to break the tie. It relied on precisely that interpretation at the Sept 17 meeting, when Noel opposed Chandrasekaran's reappointment and Srinivasan supported it.Also on Thursday's agenda is the Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group's proposal to monetise part of its 18.4% holding in Tata Sons for Rs 25,000 crore, a transaction that would alter the holding company's shareholding structure. Noel has proposed that it be implemented through a selective reduction of capital, with the shares valued under rule 11UA of the Income Tax Rules. Chandrasekaran is expected to present the board with an assessment of how Tata Sons would fund the payout, including through internal cash flows, the sale of listed investments or stake sales in newer businesses.The listing, merger and SP proposals are among seven items on the agenda. Others include dematerialisation of Tata Sons shares, including holdings of Trusts and Ratan Tata; consideration of the company's second-quarter FY27 results; business reviews of Agratas (battery venture), Tata AIG General Insurance, Tejas Networks (telecom equipment) and Air India; and a review of Tata Sons' guarantees and investments.But first the board will take up disputed minutes of Sept 17 meeting. Noel expects his objections, including his dissent over Chandrasekaran's reappointment and his interpretation of Article 121 to be reflected in the final record. Once final minutes are signed by Chandrasekaran, the board will turn to the proposals, with India Inc watching closely.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Govt implements over 250 changes for deregulation
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Fifteen months after a deregulation push, govt has implemented nearly 250 changes based on recommendations by a high-level committee led by
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Fifteen months after a deregulation push, govt has implemented nearly 250 changes based on recommendations by a high-level committee led by Niti Aayog member Rajiv Gauba, with at least 300 more changes in the pipeline and new areas, such as railways and several proposals cutting across sectors likely to be taken up in the coming months.The committee has so far submitted over a dozen reports covering MSMEs, environment, health, education, oil and gas, food safety mining, trade, pharma and IPR, among others. The implementation varies from over 50% of recommendations to a quarter of the proposals. But given the push by the PM's Office and Gauba's own initiative, including detailed consultations before the committee finalises the report, most of the recommendations will be rolled out over time, with several involving legislative changes.While there has been attention on nearly 900 provisions across laws that have been decriminalised, some of the changes to the GST rules, which were implemented last month, also flowed from the panel's recommendations.For instance, for lapses with no specific penalty, a general penalty of Rs 25,000 could be levied, irrespective of the size of business, which has now been capped at Rs 10,000. Similarly the panel sought easing of the registration process as well as simplifying the filing process for registering. Ditto for auto generation of refund acknowledgement.According to an assessment done by govt, tangible gains are flowing from the changes. For example, high-value export consignments (of Rs 10 lakh or more) through couriers have helped reduce the time to half a day instead of eight days that it took to transport by sea. Similarly, allowing e-commerce players, including overseas-controlled entities, to hold stocks for exports, is expected to translate into $4 billion additional shipments.Many of the changes are "nuts and bolt issues", officials said, meant to make life easier for businesses. For instance, the green cover required for factories in new industrial estates. Unlike the earlier prescription of 33-40% cover irrespective of the unit type, green cover set at 10% for new industrial estates, 15% for red category units and 10% for orange category, and made has been optional for green and white category units. For MSMEs in these estates, consent to notify is self-certified by them unlike earlier when they had to apply and wait for clearance. Some 15,000 renewal applications have been done away with as the consent to operate is now valid for life, and does not need to be renewed every five, 10 or 15 years.To cut the storage cost for small businesses, govt, based on the committee's recommendations, has allowed companies to share storage space for fuel, gas and chemicals from licenced entities, instead of setting up individual capacity -- a move that is expected to lower the cost for each firm to around Rs 90 crore from Rs 1.3 crore.For setting up medical education facilities, non-section 8 companies have been made eligible to apply for setting up and running colleges.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Tata Steel approves sale of tubes and pipes business
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Tata Steel board on Sunday approved proposals to sell its steel tubes and pipes business as well as Tata Steel Colors (TSCL) to APL Apollo
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tata Steel board on Sunday approved proposals to sell its steel tubes and pipes business as well as Tata Steel Colors (TSCL) to APL Apollo Tubes at a combined transaction value of about Rs 28,000 crore.The proposed sale of the steel tubes and pipes business was approved for up to Rs 11,700 crore, and the sale of the entire stake in TSCL received the nod for Rs 16,300 crore, Tata Steel said in an exchange filing.The board approved the transfer of the business of manufacturing, processing, marketing, sale, and distribution of steel tubes and pipes at and from the steel tubes manufacturing facilities of the company at Jamshedpur, Hosur, Khopoli, and Sahibabad, and certain cold rolling and surface coated steel product facilities to APL Apollo as a going concern on a slump sale basis for a lump sum consideration of up to Rs 11,700 crore.The board also approved the sale and transfer of its entire equity stake of 100% (held directly or indirectly through one of its wholly owned subsidiaries, TSDPL) in its wholly owned subsidiary, TSCL, to APL Apollo, for a consideration of about Rs 16,300 crore.The company directly holds 43.3 crore equity shares representing a 50% equity stake in its wholly owned subsidiary Tata Steel Colors (formerly known as Tata BlueScope Steel).The company, indirectly through another wholly owned subsidiary, Tata Steel Downstream Products Ltd (TSDPL), holds the remaining 43.3 crore equity shares in TSCL.Upon consummation of the transactions - proposed under the share purchase agreement - 100% of the total paid-up equity share capital of TSCL will be owned by APL Apollo, as per the filing. Both transactions are subject to customary conditions precedent, including approval from regulatory authorities as may be necessary, the company added.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Indian retail investors show strong interest in Anthropic
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Indian investors continued to trade shares of Claude maker Anthropic after its Nasdaq debut.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Indian investors continued to trade shares of Claude maker Anthropic after its Nasdaq debut. On Vested, the number of investors trading the stock rose about 46% on Friday from the first session on Thursday. Anthropic accounted for 40% of orders on INDmoney on Thursday, the platform said. Trading volume eased on Friday, though the stock continued to account for a significant share of activity, it added."We have seen strong interest from Indian investors in Anthropic since its listing. It has been among the most traded US stocks on Groww since the night of Nov 19 - the first day of trading," a Groww spokesperson told TOI.Anthropic was the second most-traded stock by value on Vested on Thursday, behind chipmaker AMD and ahead of Nvidia. The value of Anthropic shares traded was about seven times that of Nvidia, the platform said.The stock accounted for roughly 11% of Vested's total traded value and 9% of its trade count in the debut session. Nearly one in five active traders bought Anthropic shares, with the average buy order at about $1,100. Around 84% of Anthropic trades were placed within the first two hours of the stock starting to trade.On Friday, Anthropic accounted for about 6% of Vested's trade count, while the number of orders for the stock remained largely unchanged from Thursday. Around 12% of active investors traded it that day. Sell volume fell 60% from the debut session. The participation came amid sharp swings in Anthropic's share price. The stock ended Friday at $88.9, down 8.5% from Thursday's close.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Loans to micro firms have larger multiplier effect: RBI governor
articles.summary: MUMBAI: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra has called on banks to increase lending to micro enterprises and smaller economic segments, saying that disbursing Rs
articles.body: MUMBAI: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra has called on banks to increase lending to micro enterprises and smaller economic segments, saying that disbursing Rs 1,000 crore to a corporate benefits one business while lending the same amount to micro enterprises could benefit more than 10,000 families.At a financial inclusion camp in Mawal taluka, Malhotra said banks needed to extend banking and credit services to people in rural areas and smaller businesses. The camp was attended by Nidhu Saxena, MD and CEO of Bank of Maharashtra, Rajneesh Karnatak, MD and CEO of Bank of India, and Sukhwinder Kaur, DMD of SBI.Pointing out that loans to micro enterprises have a larger multiplier effect, Malhotra said financial inclusion initiatives should focus on extending banking, credit, insurance and pension services to remote areas, with greater participation of women in the formal financial system. He also stressed the need to improve digital awareness and protect customers from financial fraud. "Greater emphasis must be placed on supporting small businesses and micro-enterprises, where access to credit can improve the lives of many families," he said.Malhotra cautioned people against investment offers promising returns of 20%, 30% or even 40% over short periods, saying these were often associated with hidden risks or fraudulent schemes.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: China's $1.7 trillion AI rout turns hot trade into losing bet
articles.summary: China's AI stock trade, once a hot bet as the nation's technology powerhouses raced to catch up with the US, has morphed into a losing strategy.
articles.body: China's AI stock trade, once a hot bet as the nation's technology powerhouses raced to catch up with the US, has morphed into a losing strategy.Stocks listed on three tech-focused indexes have shed a combined $1.7 trillion in market value since the end of June, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Multifold gains in the first half of the year that pushed the likes of upstart model developer Z.AI Co and optical module maker Zhongji Innolight Co to record highs have quickly faded.The unravelling of the global AI boom has hit China particularly hard, as frothy valuations and reliance on policy support left stocks vulnerable once cracks emerged. The appeal of Chinese AI as an affordable alternative to pricier US models and the nation's pursuit of a self-sufficient chip chain is also being tested as the US tightens restrictions on technology exports.The market is set for another turbulent session on Monday, after anxiety over the viability of the AI trade turned into a full-blown rout in the US. A KraneShares exchange-traded fund tracking China's Star 50 gauge fell more than 4% in US trading.It's a painful reckoning for investors who chased China's AI rally as the 'DeepSeek moment' stunned the world.(This is a Bloomberg story)Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Small Finance Banks reduce microfin loan portfolio after stress
articles.summary: CHENNAI: Disbursements by Small Finance Banks (SFB) for microfinance are on the decline.
articles.body: CHENNAI: Disbursements by Small Finance Banks (SFB) for microfinance are on the decline. It is the fallout of stress in the microfinance sector over the past two years, which impacted net profit of several SFBs last year. Now, these institutions are diversifying their portfolios to de-risk the loan book.ESAF Small Finance Bank reported a 65% YoY (Rs 4,844 crore (Q2 FY26) vs Rs 1,704 crore (Q2 FY27)) and 28% QoQ (Rs 2,366 crore Q1 FY27) decrease in its microfinance portfolio comprising group loans. Its executive director George K John said the stress experienced by the microfinance sector over the past two-and-a-half years has reinforced the need for a more calibrated, responsible and sustainable approach to lending. "We have responded by strengthening credit underwriting, enhancing collection efficiency, monitoring household indebtedness more closely and reassessing the overall composition of our loan portfolio."However, the reduction in our traditional group-based microfinance portfolio is not merely a response to sectoral stress. It is also part of a conscious strategic transformation of our lending model. We are progressively transitioning eligible customers who have demonstrated satisfactory repayment behaviour and have moved beyond traditional microfinance requirements into our emerging household (EHL) lending segment," he told TOI.EHL caters to various categories of borrowers including individuals, small entrepreneurs and farming households. While unsecured lending within this segment is restricted to individual loans, other categories are predominantly secured.Another leading SFB player, Equitas Small Finance Bank, has brought down its microfinance exposure sharply from 20% to 12% of the total advances over the past one year. Its microfinance and micro loan advances stood at Rs 6,331 crore as of Sept 30, 2026. During an interaction three weeks ago (Nov 2, 2026), its former MD & CEO P N Vasudevan said microfinance is under control this year. "Now, about 90% of our loan book is secured," he added.Data sourced from Sa-Dhan, an association of impact finance institutions and an RBI-recognised self-regulatory organisation (SRO) for microfinance institutions (MFIs), show that the volume of loans disbursed by SFBs has reduced by 6% YoY from Rs 35,030 crore (FY25) to Rs 32,807 crore (FY26).It stood at Rs 16,541 crore in H1 FY27. Jiji Mammen, ED & CEO, Sa-Dhan, said the share of SFBs in the total microfinance portfolio remains 15% to 16%. "The only change is that their share in securitised assets is rising in percentage terms, which is also a regulatory requirement," he said. Noting that SFBs still have the same absolute microfinance portfolio size, though their percentage share must have come down, he said, "Some of these SFBs are also actively supporting MFIs through term loans or as BC partners. So, I do not see any major challenge in this."Mammen further said the stress experienced in the microfinance sector during FY25 and FY26 is a thing of the past.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Nearly half of festive sales of smartphones were financed
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Nearly one in two smartphones sold in India this festive season was bought on finance.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Nearly one in two smartphones sold in India this festive season was bought on finance. As higher memory costs pushed up handset prices, brands offered shallower discounts and leaned on no-cost EMIs to ease the upfront cost. Financing accounted for 48% of festive purchases, according to estimates from Counterpoint Research.Festive discounts narrowed to 10-25% from 35-40% a year earlier. Even after discounts, entry-level phones generally cost more than they did last year. Brands also used bank offers and trade-ins to draw shoppers, but many buyers put off upgrades. Unit sales fell 22% year on year between Oct 8 and Nov 10, almost twice the 12% drop Counterpoint had forecast. The average selling price rose 28%, keeping the market's rupee value broadly flat. Smartphone sales fell 19% year on year in the Oct 8-18 (roughly between Navratri and Dussehra) in the first wave, with online sales weaker than in earlier sale events."Buyers who needed a phone still bought one, often on EMI, but many others simply held on to what they had," said Shubham Singh, research analyst at Counterpoint. "Overall, smartphone sales this festive season were driven more by need than by festive sentiment," he added.Counterpoint had projected that financing would account for 42% of smartphone sales in 2026 as a whole, up from 35% in 2025. Its earlier tracking found that non-bank lenders accounted for about two-thirds of financed handset purchases whereas the rest came through credit- and debit-card EMIs. Financing was already common at phone shops in smaller cities before the festive sales. In April-June, buyers used EMIs for 57.5% of smartphone purchases at physical stores in tier-2 cities and for more than half in tier-3 and smaller markets.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Gold falls 11% to Rs 1.21 lakh and silver plunges 16.2% to Rs 1.47 lakh in a week to over one-year lows; analysts warn prices may slide further as US inflation data and Federal Reserve rate signals shape outlook
articles.summary: Gold price crash to continue?
articles.body: Gold price crash to continue? Gold and silver prices could face further selling pressure next week after both metals slumped to their lowest levels in more than a year. Analysts have said that investors will watch US inflation figures and signals from the Federal Reserve for indications of where interest rates are headed.Markets will also track mid-month purchasing managers’ index (PMI) readings from major economies, followed by US gross domestic product (GDP) figures, housing market data and durable goods orders. Inflation data will be particularly important in determining expectations about the Fed’s monetary policy, analysts said.Gold and silver prices crashOn the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), December gold futures shed Rs 14,927, or 11%, over the past week, settling at Rs 1,21,778 per 10 grams. The contract touched a low not seen in more than a year.Gold was last traded at a comparable level on October 30, 2025, when its price stood at Rs 1,21,508 per 10 grams, according to a PTI report.Silver futures for December delivery recorded a steeper weekly decline, losing Rs 28,496, or 16.2%, and also falling to a more than one-year low. The metal was last quoted near these levels on November 3, 2025, at Rs 1,47,758 per kg.The downturn in precious metals was equally pronounced in overseas markets. Comex gold futures lost $370.9, or 9.5%, during the week, ending at $3,515.4 per ounce. Silver futures fared worse, dropping $8.05, or 16.4%, to settle at $41.07 per ounce.Gold, silver price outlookPranav Mer, Senior Vice President, EBG -- Commodity & Currency Research at JM Financial Services Ltd, said the outlook for both precious metals remained subdued, with the ongoing decline likely to continue. He added that prices could fall further as investors evaluate fresh economic indicators and reassess the interest rate outlook.Explaining the decline in domestic gold prices, Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst -- Commodity and Currency at LKP Securities, said, "MCX gold witnessed a sharp sell-off last week, declining 11 per cent. The ongoing corrective trend extended as profit booking intensified across international and domestic bullion markets,"He added that the fall in global gold prices, alongside an appreciation in the rupee, had deepened the weakness in domestic bullion. A stronger rupee has put additional pressure on MCX prices by lowering the landed cost of imported gold.Describing the scale of the decline, Mer said, "The sell-off on bullions accelerated last week with gold falling close to $3,500 and silver at $41, both ending with a weekly loss of about 10-15 per cent, respectively,"Statements by Federal Reserve officials signalling a more hawkish approach have undermined demand for precious metals, as investors factor in the possibility of interest rates remaining elevated. The widespread decline in artificial intelligence-linked stocks has added to the selling pressure.Silver has also been hit by weakness across the industrial metals segment, with copper and zinc recording particularly sharp declines, Mer pointed out.According to him, the sell-off in equities prompted investors to liquidate bullion holdings as well, while demand for safe-haven bonds increased.The US dollar continued to hold firm, moving towards the 104 level against a basket of major currencies. Comments from Fed officials have reinforced expectations that interest rates could stay high for an extended period.Mer said, "Inflation issue is not only in US, but across most other regions, including India and we may see rate hike coming there as well. The Fed fund future are pricing in 96 per cent chance of a 25-basis-points rate hike in December,"On the geopolitical front, efforts to resolve the conflicts involving Iran and Ukraine have made little headway. Talks mediated by the US between Iran and other parties have stalled, while the outcome of last week's meeting involving Washington, Beijing and Moscow on the Ukraine conflict remains uncertain.Global bullion markets could see sharper price swings in the coming week as the Thanksgiving holiday in the US will shorten the trading week and leave markets with lower liquidity.In India, commodity markets will remain shut during the morning trading session on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own.
